Provider.limit.semantic: max simultaneous toasts; excess are marked limited (data-limited) instead of removed

Provider.toastManager.semantic: global manager so toasts can be created outside React components

Root.toast.semantic: REQUIRED — the toast object from useToastManager().toasts

Root.swipeDirection.semantic: directions in which the toast can be swiped away

Positioner.toast.semantic: REQUIRED — toast object for anchored toasts

Positioner.anchor.semantic: only Element|null here (no VirtualElement), unlike Tooltip/Popover

Positioner.align / alignOffset / sideOff.semantic: anchored toasts are opt-in via Toast.Positioner + positionerProps

Viewport.semantic: owns the stack layout; focusable region

ToastObject fields.type: { id, ref, title, type, description, timeout=5000, priority='low'|'high', transitionStatus, updateKey, limited, height, onClose, onRemove, actionProps, positionerProps, data }
ToastObject fields.semantic: priority sets aria-live politeness; updateKey increments on upsert so renderers can replay animations

ToastManager methods.type: { 'subscribe'(listener), add<T>(options) => string, close(id?), update(id, options), promise(...) }
ToastManager methods.semantic: upserting an existing id updates in place and refreshes the auto-dismiss timer

ToastManagerAddOptions.type: { id?, title?, type?, description?, timeout?, priority?, transitionStatus?, onClose?, onRemove?, actionProps?, positionerProps?, data? }

dataAttributes: Root: data-expanded, data-limited, data-swipe-direction ('up'|'down'|'left'|'right'), data-swiping, data-type (string), data-starting-style, data-ending-style
Positioner: data-anchor-hidden, data-side, data-align; CSS vars --anchor-height/width, --available-height/width, --transform-origin
Arrow: data-side, data-align, data-uncentered  (no data-open/data-closed on toast parts)
renderProp: Per-part `render` (ReactElement | (props, state) => ReactElement) via useRender, same as other Base UI parts. Toast content itself is data-driven (toast.title/description render inside Title/Description), so custom content is supplied through the manager options or by reading Toast.Root.ToastObject in the render callback.
controlled: There is no open/defaultOpen pair. Toast state lives in a ToastManager: `Toast.useToastManager()` inside components, or `Toast.createToastManager()` for a module-level manager passed to <Toast.Provider toastManager>. Add/update/close/promise (+ subscribe for events: 'add'|'close'|'update'|'promise') are the control surface; `id` upserts. Per-toast auto-dismiss via `timeout` (0 = never), and Provider.limit sets the stack cap.
formIntegration: None — no hidden inputs, no name/value submission or validation (verified across toast/*.mjs). Action/Close render native <button> elements.
keyboard: Viewport: a global keydown listener focuses it on F6 (preventDefault, remembers prevFocusElement); it renders role='region', aria-live='polite', aria-atomic=false, aria-relevant='additions text', aria-label='Notifications', tabIndex=-1. Root: Escape closes the toast — but only when focus is inside that toast's root element. No arrow-key navigation between toasts; ordering/stacking is CSS + --toast-index.
notableDifferences: No declarative state props: toasts are created imperatively through a ToastManager (useToastManager/createToastManager) and each is rendered by <Toast.Root toast={toast}>, so Toast.Root.toast is a REQUIRED prop.
No React Aria queue/region equivalents: the queue is an array from the manager plus Provider `limit`/`timeout`, and overflow is signalled with data-limited rather than removal.
Priority is a per-toast field ('low'|'high') controlling announcement urgency, not a region prop.
Anchored (positioned) toasts are a first-class mode: Toast.Positioner + Arrow with AnchorPositioning props and per-toast positionerProps — there is no React Aria analogue.
Keyboard affordance is F6-to-viewport (role=region, aria-live=polite with a hard-coded aria-label 'Notifications'), plus Escape when focus is inside the toast.
Stacking/expand visuals are pure CSS driven by --toast-index, --toast-offset-y, --toast-height, --toast-frontmost-height and data-expanded/data-behind — no built-in layout.
Promise toasts (`manager.promise`) with loading/success/error states are built in.
